title: 台风夜老宅
subject: 化学
voteQuestion: 谁的行为直接导致了本次浴室暴露事故？
background: 台风夜，老宅内发生浴室暴露事故。伤者余老师于当晚进入浴室后出现异常，随后被发现。学生需在老宅场景中搜集线索、问询人物并完成化学分析，指认直接致因者。（正式美术与完整剧情由组员提供；本配置为可玩骨架。）

危险环境取样以预先取得的模拟报告展示，不要求学生闻气味或进入危险操作。

en.title: The Typhoon-Night Old House
en.subject: Chemistry
en.voteQuestion: Whose action directly caused this bathroom exposure incident?
en.background: On a typhoon night, a bathroom exposure incident occurred in an old house. The injured person, Teacher Yu, entered the bathroom that evening, then became unwell and was found soon after. Students gather clues in the house, question the people involved, finish a chemistry analysis, and name the person whose action directly caused the exposure. (Final art and the full script come from the team; this config is a playable skeleton.)
briefing: The vote is about the action that directly caused the exposure. It is not a finding of intentional harm or a legal verdict.
Scientific conclusions must stay careful: pH, color tests, and ppm must not be over-read.
Sampling in a hazardous setting is shown through pre-collected mock reports. Students are not asked to smell anything or perform a dangerous procedure.
The medicine mock test uses tablets. TODO: names and evidence IDs in the official script, field guide, and revision list should replace this skeleton after the team confirms them.

hostNpc.name: Investigation host
hostNpc.greeting: Welcome to the typhoon-night house investigation. After the search, interviews, and chemistry analysis, wait until the teacher opens voting, then come back to me to submit the final accusation.
hostNpc.votePrompt: The teacher has opened the final vote. Choose the person whose action directly caused the incident, and fill in the evidence and the scientific reasoning. Each group may submit only once.

zhou.name: Auntie Zhou
zhou.card: Correct accusation target (skeleton). May involve mixing cleaning products. The official motive, and how much she knew, still need the team to confirm.

mockQA.q: What did you do that night?
mockQA.a: I helped tidy the cleaning products near the bathroom. I thought they were all cleaners and did not read the labels carefully.
I… may have used bottles that looked similar together. I did not know the ingredients at the time.

mockQA.q: Did you know a harmful gas might form?
mockQA.a: I only heard about the risk afterward. I really did not expect this.

mockQA.q: Where were you before the injured person entered the bathroom?
mockQA.a: I was busy with something else on the first floor. I was not watching the bathroom the whole time.

mockQA.q: Where did the cleaners come from?
mockQA.a: Some were already in the house, and some were left from an earlier purchase. A few labels had faded. — TODO: check the purchase chain against the official script.

he.name: Uncle He
he.card: A relative who often helps look after the household. The sample from the kitchen medicine box is everyday tablets (see the mock report). The report does not show whether the tablets were expired, and it does not show that Uncle He already knew.

mockQA.q: What is your relationship to the injured person?
mockQA.a: I often come to help look after things. I was in the house that night too.

mockQA.q: Were any medicine or disinfectant items involved?
mockQA.a: The kitchen medicine box holds everyday tablets. Those tablets are what the mock report tested.
I was near the kitchen. I went over after I heard a noise.

mockQA.q: Did you know some chemicals were expired or dangerous?
mockQA.a: I do not know whether the tablets were past their expiry date. Please do not turn that uncertainty into proven knowledge.

mockQA.q: Do you know about Auntie Zhou’s cleaning?
mockQA.a: She often tidies up. I did not check every detail.

lin.name: Student Lin
lin.card: TODO: the official name and movements that night follow the script.

mockQA.q: Why were you at the old house?
mockQA.a: I was staying over or visiting because of the typhoon. — TODO: confirm the setting.
I did not enter during the time of the incident.
Around 23:38 there seemed to be an unusual sound. I did not react right away.

mockQA.q: Did you see anyone near the bathroom?
mockQA.a: I remember someone moving on the first floor, but I could not tell who.
I am only a student. I would not run a dangerous experiment on my own.

wu.name: Dr. Wu
wu.card: TODO: arrival time and the boundary of the professional opinion still need confirmation. This character must not replace the students’ reasoning.

mockQA.a: I came after being contacted and helped with the first response. — TODO: exact arrival time.
It looked like exposure to an irritant gas. The final account should follow the mock tests and the scene reconstruction.

mockQA.q: Can symptoms alone establish the cause?
mockQA.a: No. You need evidence of the source, the buildup, and the exposure path.

mockQA.q: Did you move anything at the scene?
mockQA.a: First aid came first, so things may have been moved slightly. The survey record will note that.
That is not a conclusion I should give before the vote.

zhao.name: Neighbor Zhao
zhao.card: TODO: what the neighbor could see, and the timeline, still need the script.

mockQA.a: The wind was loud. I faintly heard someone call inside, then a door open.

mockQA.q: Did you see a suspicious person leave?
mockQA.a: Visibility was poor on a typhoon night. I can’t say.

mockQA.q: What do you know about this household?
mockQA.a: I know the house keeps cleaners and some old items. I don’t know the details.
About then, people were coming and going outside.
There was a faint discomfort at the door, but students must not simulate sniff-sampling in the game.

C-E01.name: Incident timeline
C-E01.studentText: Teacher Yu entered the bathroom at 23:30; an unusual sound at 23:38; found at 23:42. Injured person: Teacher Yu.

C-E02.name: Cleaner-bottle label fragments
C-E02.studentText: Empty bottles or residue of a suspected acid cleaner and a chlorine cleaner were in the same area. Placement alone does not prove they were mixed.

C-E03.name: Corridor trace
C-E03.studentText: There is a pale powdery trace on the floor. Whether it contacted the injured person needs more evidence. — TODO: shoe-powder test details still to be confirmed.

C-E04.name: First screen of the cup residue
C-E04.studentText: pH about 3, which supports that the sample is acidic. This alone cannot identify citric acid or judge how strong the acid is.

C-E05.name: Tablet color test
C-E05.studentText: The sample sent for testing is the tablets from the medicine box. The mock color test shows a color change (a classroom illustration, not a quantitative or qualitative identification). That result alone cannot prove the tablets are past their expiry date, and it cannot establish a health effect.

C-E06.name: Mixed residue in the bathroom
C-E06.studentText: The sample point shows residue features compatible with mixed cleaners (skeleton description). The exposure path still needs the ventilation and the timeline.

C-E07.name: Oxidizer first screen (P5)
C-E07.studentText: The oxidizer first screen is positive (skeleton). Keep it separate from a mock recheck that would support chlorine gas. Do not jump to a qualitative conclusion in one step.

C-E08.name: Concentration estimate note (P6)
C-E08.studentText: The model estimate of about 105 ppm is an ideal-model value, not a field measurement, and it does not by itself decide the injury. When you use the 10 ppm reference, say what it means. It is not the only safety boundary.

ph.title: Reading an acidic sample
ph.prompt: Explain what pH ≈ 3 can support, and what it cannot prove.

ppm.title: Boundaries of the ppm model
ppm.prompt: How should 105 ppm and the 10 ppm reference each be stated?

chain.title: Evidence-chain outline
chain.prompt: From source → buildup → exposure → symptoms, list your reasoning points. You do not need a character’s confession before the vote.

revealSummary.headline: Answer key: Auntie Zhou
points: The direct cause points to conduct related to improperly mixing cleaners (Auntie Zhou).
A full confession from Auntie Zhou is not required before the vote. The full account is shown after the reveal.
Scientific boundary: pH, color tests, and ppm must not be over-read.
[Skeleton] The full evidence-chain detail waits for the team’s official script.

C-E07.studentText: 氧化性初篩陽性（骨架）。需與支援氯氣存在的模擬複核區分，不能一步跳到定性結論。

C-E08.name: 濃度估算說明 (P6)
C-E08.studentText: 模型估算約 105 ppm 為理想模型值，不是現場實測，也不直接決定具體傷情。使用 10 ppm 參考值時須說明含義，非唯一安全邊界。
